subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing cadence guardrail, with unset/0 preserving shipped behavior and configured values rejecting or pacing fast recurring jobs?
rationale: The implementation is default-off, but it adds a core config surface and deliberate fail-closed schedule validation/runtime pacing for configured deployments, which automation should not accept without maintainer product intent.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Repair
options.body: Keep the core config surface, require the generated docs-map fix and fresh exact-head checks, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

options.title: Prefer Warning-Only Policy
options.body: Reject enforcement for now and use a warning-only approach like the closed high-frequency cron proposal if maintainers do not want configured schedule rejection.

options.title: Defer Core Config Surface
options.body: Pause or close this PR until a broader cron/operator resource policy decides where cadence guardrails belong.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Repair
recommendation.body: Keep the core config surface, require the generated docs-map fix and fresh exact-head checks, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned and the remaining blocker is a product/compatibility decision about accepting a new core cron config guardrail.
